name: A ripple that follows your cursor, tuned live in the panel
object: Interactive Shaders in Framer, starting with the Ripple Shader, a WebGL effect that distorts an image with water-like ripples that follow the cursor and respond to clicks and drags
audience: designers building motion-led, experimental sites who want real-time interactive effects without writing shader code
message: This video tells designers that a cursor-reactive WebGL effect is now just a property panel away, tunable in real time with no shader code required.

moments.what: a glowing Framer glyph distorts into ripples as the narrator introduces the feature over the effect applied to the logo itself
moments.copy: We're bringing interactive shaders to Framer, starting with the Ripple Shader.

moments.what: a property panel appears beside a live canvas showing radius, fade, strength, decay, displacement and dispersion sliders, each one reshaping the ripple around the cursor as it's dragged
moments.copy: Through properties like radius, strength, decay, displacement and dispersion, you can customize the ripple's size, intensity, motion and color split.

moments.what: the effect is shown following the cursor automatically on hover, then a spring-based transition curve is opened and tuned, blending motion-style physics with the WebGL shader
moments.copy: These interactive shaders support spring-based cursor tracking, blending motion-style interaction with WebGL shaders.

moments.what: two more behaviors are demonstrated: an optional click property that sends ripples outward on click, and a click-drag that amplifies the ripple for a heavier, more physical feel
moments.copy: We have an optional click property that sends ripples out as you click the image, and if you click-drag, the ripple effect is amplified.

moments.what: closes with the feature confirmed live and the Framer glyph on black
moments.copy: The Ripple Shader is out now in Framer. Thank you for watching, and stay tuned for more updates coming soon.

cta: "The Ripple Shader is out now in Framer", delivered as a direct narration line over the glyph, closing with a tease of more shaders to come
why: Walking through each property slider live, on the same canvas, while naming exactly what it changes turns a single buzzword, interactive shaders, into something a designer can picture tuning themselves within seconds of watching.
